title: Inequalities and Systems of Inequalities
subtitle: Translate limits, solve inequalities, graph solution regions, and model real-world constraints.

isi.content: An equation usually describes an exact value. An inequality describes a range of values that satisfy a condition. SAT Math inequalities often model budgets, capacities, minimum requirements, maximum limits, and time or distance restrictions.

rows: at least / no less than / minimum
at most / no more than / maximum

isi.content: Translate the phrase before doing arithmetic. “Under 325” means strictly less than 325, while “no more than 325” means less than or equal to 325.
Solve an inequality using the same balance principle as an equation. There is one special rule: whenever you multiply or divide by a negative number, reverse the inequality sign.

isi.title: Example: positive divisor
isi.content: Solve \(5x-7\le18\). Add 7 to get \(5x\le25\), then divide by positive 5: \(x\le5\).

isi.title: Example: negative divisor
isi.content: Solve \(1-2x\ge-1\). Subtract 1 to get \(-2x\ge-2\). Dividing by \(-2\) reverses the sign, so \(x\le1\).
Adding or subtracting a number does not reverse the sign. Only multiplication or division by a negative number reverses it.

A compound inequality combines two conditions. The word “and” means both conditions must be true, so the solution is an intersection. The word “or” means at least one condition is true, so the solution is a union.

items.title: And
items.content: “At least 12 but less than 30” becomes \(12\le n<30\).

items.title: Or
items.content: “Less than 5 or greater than 10” becomes \(x<5\) or \(x>10\).

items.title: Interval meaning
items.content: A closed endpoint is included; an open endpoint is excluded.

isi.title: Example: a bounded quantity
isi.content: If a club has at least 40 members but no more than 75 members, then \(40\le m\le75\). Both endpoints are included.
A system of inequalities describes values that satisfy every condition at the same time. Its solution is the overlap of the individual solution sets.

isi.title: Example: work hours and earnings
isi.content: If tutoring pays USD \(12\) per hour and lifeguarding pays USD \(9.50\) per hour, a student works no more than 20 hours and wants at least USD \(220\), then \(\begin{cases}12x+9.5y\ge220\\x+y\le20\end{cases}\).

items: Define each variable and include units.
Use the correct inequality direction for each phrase.
Check the final point or region against every condition.

isi.content: For counts of people, boxes, or items, include nonnegative and whole-number restrictions when the context requires them.
A solid boundary includes points on the line, so it represents \(\le\) or \(\ge\). A dashed boundary excludes the line, so it represents \(<\) or \(>\).

isi.title: Example: test a point
isi.content: To test whether \((2,-1)\) satisfies \(y\le3x+1\), substitute: \(-1\le7\), which is true. If the point is not on the boundary, testing \((0,0)\) can also reveal which side should be shaded.
Build the quantity model first, then compare it with the limit. Keep units consistent and interpret the final result in context.

isi.title: Example: weight capacity
isi.content: An empty truck weighs 4,500 pounds, each box weighs 14 pounds, and the bridge limit is 6,000 pounds. The total must remain below the limit: \(4500+14x<6000\). Thus \(x<\dfrac{1500}{14}\approx107.14\), so the maximum whole number of boxes is 107.

isi.title: Example: distance
isi.content: If one driver travels at 37 miles per hour for \(r\) hours and another travels at 43 miles per hour for \(j\) hours, and their total distance is under 325 miles, then \(37r+43j<325\).

items: Round down for a maximum whole-number capacity when the exact upper bound is not an integer.
Do not round up if doing so violates a strict limit.
Keep money, distance, time, weight, and item counts in compatible units.

isi.content: A total may contain a fixed amount plus a percentage of another quantity. Translate the total first, then apply the lower and upper limits.

isi.title: Example: commission interval
isi.content: If earnings are \(E=x+0.11s\), where \(x\) is base salary and \(s\) is sales, and earnings must satisfy \(3x\le E\le4x\), then \(3x\le x+0.11s\le4x\). Subtracting \(x\) gives \(2x\le0.11s\le3x\), so \(\dfrac{2}{0.11}x\le s\le\dfrac{3}{0.11}x\).

isi.title: Example: tax-inclusive budget
isi.content: If a business buys \(n\) chairs at a pre-tax price \(p\), and 7% sales tax is included in a USD \(14{,}000\) budget, the model is \(1.07np\le14{,}000\).

items: Substitute a candidate point into every inequality in a system.
Test boundary values to decide whether equality is included.
Check whether the answer has the correct sign, units, and domain.
Use Desmos to enter each inequality separately and inspect the overlap.
When graphing, verify that the viewing window includes the relevant region.

isi.content: A calculator can display a solution region, but it cannot decide whether the original wording means “at least,” “more than,” or “no more than.”

latihan.question: Rhett drives at 37 miles per hour for \(r\) hours and Jessica drives at 43 miles per hour for \(j\) hours. Their total distance is under 325 miles. Which inequality represents the situation?
discussion: Distance equals rate multiplied by time, so the distances are \(37r\) and \(43j\).
The correct inequality is \(37r+43j<325\), choice B.

latihan.question: Which inequality is equivalent to \(6x-9y>12\)?
discussion: Divide every term by the positive number 3.
Because the divisor is positive, the inequality sign does not change. Choice B is correct.

latihan.question: Given \(y>2x-1\) and \(2x>5\), which describes all possible \(y\)-coordinates?
discussion: Therefore, \(2x-1>4\). Since \(y>2x-1\), every possible y-coordinate must satisfy \(y>4\).
The correct answer is choice B.

latihan.question: An essay may have no more than 5,000 words and already has 3,026 words. What is the maximum number of additional words?
discussion: Let \(w\) be the number of additional words. The limit is \(3026+w\le5000\).
Therefore, the maximum number of additional words is 1,974, choice A.

latihan.question: If \(x+6>0\) and \(1-2x\ge-1\), which value is not a solution?
discussion: Together, \(-6<x\le1\). The value \(-6\) is excluded, so choice A is not a solution.

latihan.question: A plant is classified as tall if its height \(h\) is more than 120 centimeters. Which interval represents possible heights of a tall plant?
discussion: A tall plant must have height greater than 120 centimeters.
Only the interval \(112<h<165\) contains heights greater than 120.

latihan.question: A truck weighs 4,500 pounds empty. Each box weighs 14 pounds. The bridge limit is 6,000 pounds, and the total must remain below the limit. What is the maximum whole number of boxes?
discussion: Because the number of boxes must be a whole number and the limit is strict, the maximum is 107.

latihan.question: A venue charges USD \(35\) plus USD \(10.25\) per attendee. The budget is USD \(300\). What is the greatest possible whole number of attendees?
discussion: Thus \(a\le25.85\ldots\). Since attendees are whole people, the greatest possible number is 25.

latihan.question: Annual energy costs fall from USD \(4,334\) to USD \(2,712\) after a USD \(25,000\) installation. Which inequality determines when the savings exceed the installation cost after \(t\) years?
discussion: Savings exceed the installation cost when \(1622t>25,000\).
This is equivalent to \(25,000<(4,334-2,712)t\), choice B.

latihan.question: Total earnings are a base salary \(x\) plus 11% of sales \(s\). Earnings must be at least \(3x\) and at most \(4x\). Which interval describes possible sales?
A business has a USD \(14,000\) budget for 81 chairs, including 7% sales tax. What is the maximum pre-tax price per chair, rounded to the nearest cent?
discussion: If \(p\) is the pre-tax price per chair, the tax-inclusive total is \(81(1.07p)\).
Set the total equal to the budget: \(81(1.07p)=14,000\).
The maximum pre-tax price is USD 161.53, choice B.

latihan.question: Forklift boxes weigh 40 or 65 pounds. The forklift can carry at most 45 boxes or 2,400 pounds. If \(x\) and \(y\) count the two types of boxes, which system represents the situation?
Jackie earns USD \(12\) per hour tutoring and USD \(9.50\) per hour lifeguarding, works no more than 20 hours, and wants at least USD \(220\). Which system represents the situation?
discussion: The correct system is choice C.

latihan.question: Given \(y\le3x+1\) and \(x-y>1\), which ordered pair satisfies the system?
discussion: Test \((2,-1)\): the first inequality is \(-1\le3(2)+1=7\), true.
Therefore, choice D satisfies the system.

latihan.question: T-shirts cost USD \(8\) and water bottles cost USD \(5\). Revenue must be at least USD \(140\), with no more than 24 items. Which point \((x,y)\), representing shirts and bottles, is in the solution region?
discussion: For \((16,6)\), revenue is \(8(16)+5(6)=158\), and the item count is \(16+6=22\). Both conditions are satisfied.
Therefore, the correct point is \((16,6)\), choice C.

latihan.question: In an experiment, 36 of the first 150 participants chose the first picture. Of the remaining 150, \(p\) did so. More than 20% of all 300 participants must choose it. Which system represents the situation?
discussion: The total number choosing the picture is \(36+p\).
Since \(p\) counts people in the remaining group, \(p\le150\).
The correct system is choice D.

latihan.question: Marisa needs at least 10 staff: junior directors cost USD \(640\) per week and senior directors cost USD \(880\) per week. The budget is at most USD \(9,700\); at least 3 juniors and 1 senior are required. Which system represents the situation?
discussion: The minimum staffing requirements are \(x\ge3\) and \(y\ge1\).

latihan.question: A rectangular-prism box has height 60 inches, length 2.5 times its width \(x\), and the perimeter of the base plus the height is no greater than 130 inches. Which inequality describes \(x\)?
discussion: The width is \(x\) and the length is \(2.5x\).
Because a width must be positive, \(0<x\le10\), choice A.

additionalPractice.question: Which inequality means “at least 18”?
discussion: “At least” includes the boundary value and means greater than or equal to.
The correct inequality is \(x\ge18\), choice B.

additionalPractice.question: A box weighs 6 pounds and an empty truck weighs 420 pounds. If the limit is 600 pounds, write an inequality for the number \(x\) of boxes.
discussion: The total weight is the empty-truck weight plus the box weight: \(420+6x\).
The truck cannot exceed 600 pounds, so \(420+6x\le600\).

additionalPractice.question: Solve \(-4x+9>25\).
discussion: Divide by \(-4\) and reverse the inequality: \(x<-4\).

additionalPractice.question: A club has at least 40 members but no more than 75 members. Write a compound inequality.
A tutoring service charges USD \(20\) plus USD \(15\) per hour. The budget is USD \(140\). What is the greatest possible number of whole hours?
discussion: Divide by 15: \(h\le8\). Therefore, the greatest whole number is 8 hours.

additionalPractice.question: A student works no more than 18 hours. Tutoring pays USD \(14\) per hour and laboratory work pays USD \(11\) per hour. The student wants to earn at least USD \(220\). Write a system for tutoring hours \(t\) and laboratory hours \(\ell\).
Determine whether \((3,2)\) satisfies \(\begin{cases}y\ge x-1\\2x+y<10\end{cases}\).
discussion: Check the first inequality: \(2\ge3-1\), so \(2\ge2\), true.
The point satisfies both inequalities, so the answer is yes.

additionalPractice.question: A school orders notebooks and folders. Notebooks cost USD \(2\) and folders cost USD \(3\). The school can spend at most USD \(180\) and must order at least 70 items. Write a system for notebooks \(n\) and folders \(f\).
discussion: Together, these inequalities model the situation.
